questions.q: What does journal import actually do?
options: It deletes journal batches that are no longer needed
It takes journal data arriving from an external or semi-external source and creates it as a properly structured GL journal batch
It validates an Application Accounting Definition
It calculates depreciation for Fixed Assets
questions.explain: Journal import is the mechanism that converts incoming journal data into a standard GL journal batch with a batch name, source, category, and other attributes.

questions.q: Is journal import a mechanism built exclusively for Subledger Accounting?
options: Yes, it exists solely to serve Subledger Accounting and nothing else
No, it is only used for Fixed Assets depreciation
Journal import does not exist in Oracle Fusion
No — it is a general-purpose GL mechanism also used for spreadsheet uploads, FBDI files, and feeds from non-Oracle systems; SLA is simply its highest-volume user
questions.explain: Journal import is shared across multiple sources of journal data; Subledger Accounting is the most common, highest-volume user of it, not the only one.

questions.q: What do the source and category attributes on a GL journal batch represent?
options: A random internal identifier with no business meaning
Which system or process the journal came from (source) and the type of activity it represents (category), such as "Payables" and "Purchase Invoices"
The user who manually typed the journal entry
The exchange rate used for currency conversion
questions.explain: Source identifies the originating system or process, and category identifies the type of activity, letting journals be filtered and reported by origin.

questions.q: How do the source and category on a GL journal batch relate to concepts from Chapter 1?
options: They are unrelated to anything covered earlier in the course
They only apply to manually entered journal entries, never to subledger-originated ones
They replace the need for an accounting method
They trace directly back to the event class and subledger application that originally raised the accounting event
questions.explain: The classification set up at the very start of the course (event class, subledger application) remains visible at the GL journal level through source and category.

questions.q: If Create Accounting ran successfully in Final mode but no corresponding journal appears in General Ledger, what does this lesson suggest checking?
options: Nothing can be checked; this situation is unexplainable
Only the Chart of Accounts segment structure
The GL journal batch list, filtered by source, category, ledger, and date, to see whether journal import actually created the batch or the issue is further upstream
The ledger's functional currency setting
questions.explain: Filtering the GL journal batch list helps determine whether journal import succeeded or whether the problem lies upstream in Create Accounting or the transfer step.
